title: Related Questions
question: Related Questions Q. I am a newly married couple and wish to learn about the sunnah and practices of the families of Rasulullah s.a.w. and his companions in regards to breast-feeding their children. How long should we feed mother's milk to boys and girls? 4025 views Q. I have heard that fictional stories are permissible to read and write, but I wasn?t sure under which circumstances. Now, I've noticed, that many youth are writing fiction. Some stories I've noticed contain haram love, killing and fabricating creatures and worlds. I?ve been writing but this question has been bugging me for a very long time. So I wanted to go into detail a bit about fiction writing Are these permissible? 1. Is fabricating worlds, lands (i.e such as the lands of Middle Earth by Tolkien or Narnia by Lewis.) and creatures permissible? 2. Having bloodshed (including against non-existent creatures). 3. In detail describing characters of the opposite gender (a male writer describing the complexion and characteristics of a female character, or a female writer describing a male character). 4. Unlawful situations taking place (an obvious one is kissing, but how about a character killing in rage?) does it make the story unlawful to write? 5. Finally, what if the story ends up with a message, or situations the character(s) go through which teaches or shows a person right from wrong (Including the above four) Considering these factors, is writing still permissible? 3979 views Q. answer: Social Matters >> Education & Upbringing Question ID: 35887 Country: India Title: My sister got married on 19 Feb. Her husband was later found very cheap, vulgar and he also used to beat my sister badly just for his pleasure and there was also fear that he will kill her Question: My sister got married on 19 Feb. Her husband was later found very cheap, vulgar and he also used to beat my sister badly just for his pleasure and there was also fear that he will kill her. So my family demanded for divorce and on 17 Sept she got divorced. But she was pregnant at that time and she gave birth to a son on 25 Nov but my family forced my sister's in-laws (sasural) to keep that child and just few hours after birth they handed over newly born infant to them. In my opinion it was zulm. Are my sister and my family not zalim in this case? Mother must take care of her child at least when he need breast feed. Am I right or wrong? Please give references otherwise my family will not agree. Answer ID: 35887 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 98/81/B=1433) The right of child nourishment goes to mother. She shall nourish the child up to seven years and shall take its expenses from husband. It is not right for her to give the child to the father before this period. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
